title: Boss: the payments encryption layer
summary: Load keys safely, tokenize card numbers, envelope-encrypt records under versioned KEKs, and rotate without downtime.

steps.title: The job
body: You own the encryption layer of a payments service. It must load its keys without ever falling back to a default, keep card numbers out of most of the system with tokens, store records with envelope encryption under versioned key-encryption keys, and rotate those keys without re-encrypting data or breaking old records.
As always here, keys and nonces in the tests are fixed so results repeat; the prompts say where real code uses randomness.

steps.title: Load the key ring from the environment
prompt: The platform hands your service its configuration as `NAME=value` lines on standard input (read to the end). Lines without `=` and lines whose name does not start with `KEK_` are ignored. Split each line at the **first** `=` only (Base64 contains `=`).
- `KEK_<id>=<base64>` defines a key with that id (for example `KEK_v1`).
- `KEK_CURRENT=<id>` names the key that encrypts new data.
Check in this order and print exactly one line:
1. no `KEK_CURRENT`: `error: KEK_CURRENT is missing`
2. for each key id in ordinal order: invalid Base64 gives `error: key <id> is not valid base64`, and a length other than 32 bytes gives `error: key <id> must be 32 bytes, got <n>`
3. `KEK_CURRENT` names no defined key: `error: KEK_CURRENT names unknown key <id>`
4. otherwise: `loaded <count> keys (<ids, ordinal, comma-space separated>), current <id>`
Never print a key value.
steps.starter: // Read NAME=value lines from standard input.
solution: if (!values.TryGetValue("KEK_CURRENT", out var current)) return "error: KEK_CURRENT is missing";
var ids = values.Keys.Where(k => k != "KEK_CURRENT").Select(k => k[4..]).OrderBy(k => k, StringComparer.Ordinal).ToList();
catch (FormatException) { return $"error: key {id} is not valid base64"; }
if (key.Length != 32) return $"error: key {id} must be 32 bytes, got {key.Length}";
if (!ids.Contains(current)) return $"error: KEK_CURRENT names unknown key {current}";

tests.name: a short key
tests.expect: error: key v2 must be 32 bytes, got 16

tests.name: junk Base64
tests.expect: error: key v1 is not valid base64

tests.name: current names an unknown key
tests.expect: error: KEK_CURRENT names unknown key v3

hints: `line.IndexOf('=')` then `line[..eq]` and `line[(eq + 1)..]` splits at the first `=` only.
Collect everything first, then validate: the order of the input lines must not change the answer.

steps.title: Tokenize card numbers for the dashboard
prompt: Support staff must see *which* card a customer used without ever seeing the number. Write, as top-level code:
- `string Mask(string pan)`: `"**** **** **** "` followed by the last four digits.

- `string Tokenize(string pan)`: `"tok_"` + 32 lowercase hex characters from `RandomNumberGenerator`; the same card always returns the same token. Reject a `pan` that is not 13 to 19 ASCII digits with `ArgumentException`.
- `string Detokenize(string token, string role)`: only role `"payments"` may detokenize; any other role throws `UnauthorizedAccessException`. Unknown tokens throw `KeyNotFoundException`.
solution: throw new ArgumentException("A card number is 13 to 19 digits.");
if (tokenByPan.TryGetValue(pan, out var existing)) return existing;
if (role != "payments") throw new UnauthorizedAccessException("Only the payments service may detokenize.");
template: {{CODE}}
var dojoT = Tokenize("4111111111111111");
Dojo.Check("tokens are tok_ + 32 hex", dojoT.Length == 36 && dojoT.StartsWith("tok_"), dojoT);
Dojo.Eq("the same card, the same token", dojoT, Tokenize("4111111111111111"));
Dojo.Eq("payments can detokenize", "4111111111111111", Detokenize(dojoT, "payments"));
Dojo.Throws<UnauthorizedAccessException>("support cannot detokenize", () => Detokenize(dojoT, "support"));
Dojo.Throws<KeyNotFoundException>("unknown tokens are refused", () => Detokenize("tok_ffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffff", "payments"));
Dojo.Throws<ArgumentException>("letters are not a card number", () => Tokenize("4111-1111-1111-1111"));
Dojo.Throws<ArgumentException>("12 digits is too short", () => Tokenize("411111111111"));
hints: Check the role before touching the dictionary, so an unauthorised caller learns nothing, not even whether the token exists.

steps.title: Envelope records under versioned KEKs
prompt: The starter has the key ring (`keks`) and the id of the current KEK (`current`). Records are stored as one string:
```text
<kekId>.<Base64 of wrapped DEK>.<Base64 of encrypted data>
Both Base64 parts are nonce (12) + ciphertext + tag (16) from AES-GCM. Write:
- `string Encrypt(string text, byte[] dek, byte[] dekNonce, byte[] dataNonce)`: wrap the DEK under `keks[current]`, encrypt the text under the DEK.
- `string Decrypt(string blob)`: use the KEK named in the blob, whatever `current` is now. A blob that is not three parts throws `FormatException`; an unknown KEK id throws `KeyNotFoundException`.
(In production the DEK is `RandomNumberGenerator.GetBytes(32)` and both nonces are random; the tests pass them in.)
starter: ["v1"] = Enumerable.Repeat((byte)1, 32).ToArray(),   // in real life: unwrapped by the KMS
solution: ["v1"] = Enumerable.Repeat((byte)1, 32).ToArray(),   // in real life: unwrapped by the KMS
byte[] Box(byte[] key, byte[] nonce, byte[] plain)
gcm.Encrypt(nonce, plain, box.AsSpan(12, plain.Length), box.AsSpan(12 + plain.Length));
string Encrypt(string text, byte[] dek, byte[] dekNonce, byte[] dataNonce)
if (parts.Length != 3) throw new FormatException("A blob has three parts.");
template: {{CODE}}
var dojoDek = Enumerable.Range(1, 32).Select(i => (byte)(i * 3)).ToArray();
byte[] DojoN(byte n) { var b = new byte[12]; b[11] = n; return b; }
var dojoBlob = Encrypt("charge 19.99 EUR", dojoDek, DojoN(1), DojoN(2));
Dojo.Check("the blob starts with the current KEK id", dojoBlob.StartsWith("v1."), dojoBlob);
Dojo.Eq("the blob has three parts", 3, dojoBlob.Split('.').Length);
Dojo.Eq("the wrapped DEK is 60 bytes", 60, Convert.FromBase64String(dojoBlob.Split('.')[1]).Length);
Dojo.Eq("Decrypt gives the text back", "charge 19.99 EUR", Decrypt(dojoBlob));
current = "v2";
Dojo.Eq("old records still decrypt after the current key changes", "charge 19.99 EUR", Decrypt(dojoBlob));
Dojo.Check("new records use v2", Encrypt("x", dojoDek, DojoN(3), DojoN(4)).StartsWith("v2."), "still v1");
Dojo.Throws<KeyNotFoundException>("an unknown KEK id is refused", () => Decrypt("v7" + dojoBlob[2..]));
Dojo.Throws<FormatException>("a malformed blob is refused", () => Decrypt("v1.abc"));
var dojoParts = dojoBlob.Split('.');
var dojoData = Convert.FromBase64String(dojoParts[2]); dojoData[13] ^= 1;
Dojo.Throws<System.Security.Cryptography.AuthenticationTagMismatchException>("a tampered record is detected", () => Decrypt($"{dojoParts[0]}.{dojoParts[1]}.{Convert.ToBase64String(dojoData)}"));
hints: Write `Box(key, nonce, plain)` and `Unbox(key, box)` helpers, then `Encrypt` is three lines.
Base64 never contains `.`, so `blob.Split('.')` is safe; check for exactly three parts.

steps.title: Rotate without downtime
prompt: Your key ring now rotates. Starting from the previous step's code, add:

- `string Rewrap(string blob, byte[] nonce)`: if the blob already uses `current`, return it unchanged. Otherwise unwrap its DEK with its own KEK and return `"<current>.<new wrapped DEK>.<same data part>"`: the data part must be **the exact same text** as before.
- `bool CanRetire(IEnumerable<string> blobs, string kekId)`: `true` only if `kekId` is not current and no blob still uses it.
The tests store records under v1, rotate to v2, check that v1 cannot be retired yet, rewrap everything, and then retire it.

template: {{CODE}}
byte[] DojoN(byte n) { var b = new byte[12]; b[11] = n; return b; }
var dojoBlobs = new List<string>
Encrypt("record one", Enumerable.Repeat((byte)7, 32).ToArray(), DojoN(1), DojoN(2)),
Encrypt("record two", Enumerable.Repeat((byte)8, 32).ToArray(), DojoN(3), DojoN(4)),
current = "v2";
Dojo.Check("v1 cannot be retired while records use it", !CanRetire(dojoBlobs, "v1"), "CanRetire said yes too early");
var dojoBefore = dojoBlobs.Select(b => b.Split('.')[2]).ToList();
dojoBlobs = dojoBlobs.Select((b, i) => Rewrap(b, DojoN((byte)(10 + i)))).ToList();
Dojo.Check("rewrapped records use v2", dojoBlobs.All(b => b.StartsWith("v2.")), string.Join(" ", dojoBlobs.Select(b => b[..2])));
Dojo.Eq("the data parts are untouched", dojoBefore, dojoBlobs.Select(b => b.Split('.')[2]).ToList());
Dojo.Eq("records still decrypt", "record two", Decrypt(dojoBlobs[1]));
Dojo.Eq("rewrapping a current blob changes nothing", dojoBlobs[0], Rewrap(dojoBlobs[0], DojoN(99)));
Dojo.Check("now v1 can be retired", CanRetire(dojoBlobs, "v1"), "CanRetire said no");
Dojo.Check("the current key can never be retired", !CanRetire(dojoBlobs, "v2"), "CanRetire allowed retiring the current key");
keks.Remove("v1");
Dojo.Eq("after retiring v1, everything still decrypts", "record one", Decrypt(dojoBlobs[0]));
hints: `Rewrap` splits the blob, returns it as-is when `parts[0] == current`, and otherwise rebuilds it from `current`, a new wrapped DEK and `parts[2]`.
